1.explanation:
• content-switcher.js: defines the markup and class names for selected vs. unselected tabs. It determines which CSS classes are applied and may need to expose new class hooks (e.g. for a stronger border) or adjust the light variant logic.
• content-switcher.config.js: holds the tokens and props mapping for theming and usage guidelines. If the fix involves switching tokens (e.g. raising border color from ui-03 to ui-04) this is the place to update default values.
• _content-switcher.scss: contains the actual styles for .bx--content-switcher-btn and .bx--content-switcher-btn--selected. The light grey background and border color are defined here; they need to be updated to darker tones or a stronger stroke that meets 3:1 contrast.
• React wrapper (ContentSwitcher.js): applies the light/regular variant prop to the underlying Vanilla JS component. If a new prop (e.g. for high-contrast outline) is introduced or default class names change, this wrapper must be updated to pass it through.
1.bug_scenario: The ContentSwitcher component’s unselected tabs use a very light grey background (#f4f4f4) and a pale grey border (#e0e0e0). Against the container background these colors only achieve about 1.1:1 contrast, far below the 3:1 minimum required by WCAG 1.4.11 for “visual information required to identify user interface components.” In practice this makes the group of tabs look like a standalone black button and plain text, especially in two-tab implementations. The selected tab (black background) meets contrast, but the light-on-lighter styling of unselected tabs fails.

2.explanation:
All of the above files contribute to how the ContentSwitcher is styled, themed, and tested across the Carbon library.

• styles/scss/components/_content-switcher.scss holds the SASS rules that define the background color, border color, and divider color for both selected and unselected tabs. This is where the low-contrast grey values (#f4f4f4 background, #e0e0e0 border) must be bumped to darker shades that meet at least 3:1 contrast.

• packages/components/src/components/content-switcher/content-switcher.config.js declares the design tokens and CSS custom properties for the component. If new color variables (e.g. a higher-contrast stroke or divider) are needed, they should be added here so that themes and the vanilla JS version can consume them.

• packages/components/src/components/content-switcher/content-switcher.js (the vanilla-JS implementation) applies the CSS classes and inline styles defined by the config, so it may need adjustment to support any new contrast-focused modifiers (for example toggling a new “high-contrast‐border” class on unselected switches).

• packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher.js is the React wrapper of the component and is responsible for passing through the correct classNames (including light/dark variants). If a new CSS class or prop (e.g. a “highContrast” flag) is introduced, the React component must reflect that change.

• packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher-test.js contains the snapshot/unit tests for the React component. After any markup or className changes, these tests must be updated to expect the new class or style output.

• packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher-story.js defines the Storybook example. Once the contrast styles are updated, the demo should render with the updated border and divider colors so designers and consumers can preview the fix.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering a two‐tab ContentSwitcher on a light grey background, the unselected tab’s fill and border are too light to meet WCAG 1.4.11. The pale grey background (#f4f4f4) and border (#e0e0e0) only achieve about 1.1:1 contrast against the parent background—far below the required 3:1 ratio. As a result, unselected tabs and the divider bar are almost invisible in low‐resolution or noisy contexts, causing users to misinterpret the component (e.g. perceiving the selected “All” tab as an isolated black button).
